The [original BERT4Rec paper, §§3.5–3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2), specifies bidirectional masked-item reconstruction, full-item softmax with tied input/output embeddings, additional last-item-only masking examples, and inference by appending [MASK] and reading its hidden state. It discusses enumerating every next-item prefix as an expensive alternative—not its prescribed training procedure. Shifted targets with unmasked bidirectional inputs leak answers.

The [official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py) uses complete histories when short and overlapping fixed-length windows when long; default stride is 0.1×maximum length, not every prefix. It creates dupe_factor random-mask copies plus one last-item-only example per window. Random targets number min(max_predictions_per_seq, max(1, round(length×masked_lm_prob))), guaranteeing at least one eligible target for nonempty item sequences under normal positive settings. Its mask_prob default is 1.0: selected targets become [MASK], despite inherited comments describing 80/10/10 replacement. Distinguish the paper’s item-only softmax from executable code: [run.py](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py) normalizes over every embedding row; [vocab.py](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/vocab.py) defines N+4 rows: N items, three special tokens, and ID zero. Special classes therefore participate in training normalization, although recommendation candidates are items.

[Petrov and Macdonald’s RecSys 2022 replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) found default configurations undertrained: reproducing original results required up to 30× longer training; their implementation reproduced three of four datasets with up to 95% less convergence time. Their [recency-sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) explicitly links random-mask/terminal-mask mismatch to slow convergence. [Klenitskiy and Vasilev, RecSys 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602), demonstrate that full-softmax versus sampled loss materially changes accuracy and training speed. These establish consequential implementation/training choices, not isolated causal ablations of every detail above; host-baseline integration still needs separate verification.
